transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Park (Redwood SE), Maya Reyes (Sentinel Head of ML), Owen Li (Infra Lead), Priya Kumar (CTO)

Summary: Quick Optimize walkthrough centering on quantization profiles (INT8/FP8). Maya outlined production latency goals (p95 < 350ms) and quality tolerances (acceptable hallucination rate < 2% on extraction tasks). Redwood team demoed the Optimize UI and walked through benchmark deltas.

Topics: INT8 vs FP8, quality regression monitoring, KV cache impacts, batching, dedicated vs hosted economics, security and compliance.

Action items (captured in metadata): see action_items field.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Avery, AE on the Redwood Optimize team, jordan is our systems engineer, he'll run through the quant profiles and benchmarks. how are we looking on time?
[00:24] Maya Reyes: good here, thanks. we're most interested in how much latency we can shave and how quality holds up for our RAG pipeline, we run relatively long prompts, about 1k tokens on average.
[00:35] Jordan Park: great, that's helpful. i'll start with a quick slide then jump into the console. just to set expectations INT8 is usually lower latency and cost, FP8 tends to keep quality higher esp on longer context and dense language tasks. but results are model-and-workload dependent.
[01:10] Owen Li: can you clarify model variants? like which models you tested int8/fp8 on?
[01:18] Jordan Park: yeah we ran this across a few open models in our catalog — the 7B/13B family and a tuned 34B variant for comparison. note, some vendor names and model labels in the transcript might be off — we used Redwood-verified profiles.
[01:45] Maya Reyes: our main concern is p95 latency under load; cost is important but if responses are bad that's a showstopper.
[01:55] Avery Chen: totally. for your p95 target of ~350ms, with 13B class models and INT8 profiles we were seeing median latencies ~180ms and p95 ~320ms on our dedicated config with optimized kernels; FP8 bumped p95 to ~420-480ms in some runs but quality improved on instruction following.
[02:30] Jordan Park: (screen share) here's Optimize — you can select quant profile, see per-token latency and a quality delta metric we compute from eval sets. the UI also surfaces a quality vs latency curve.
[03:05] Maya Reyes: that curve's useful, how do you compute 'quality delta'? is it BLEU, ROUGE, or custom?
[03:14] Jordan Park: it's flexible — for these demos we used a mix: embedding similarity + exact match on extraction tasks and a human-eval proxy for instruction adherence. might be noisy, but it correlates well. also note our eval harness supports your custom prompt set.
[03:45] Priya Kumar: on security — we need KMS integrations and audit logs. can the private deployment run Optimize with customer-managed keys?
[03:56] Avery Chen: yes, Private supports customer managed KMS/HSM and audit logs. Dedicated gets you data isolation and VPC peering; Hosted has encryption at rest but we can't support customer-managed keys in hosted tenancy.
[04:18] Owen Li: for pilot we'll likely need VPC + KMS. is that supported in the trial?
[04:25] Jordan Park: we can do a pilot in a Dedicated environment or Private staging with your KMS; it requires a bit more setup but we have a runbook. i'll send that as part of next steps.
[05:00] Jordan Park: diving back into benchmarks — here's INT8 vs FP8 on a retrieval-augmented set. INT8 reduced token compute by ~2.8x at batch=4, and latency dropped ~30% in these runs. FP8 kept the exact-match for extraction up by ~3-4 percentage points on average.
[05:40] Maya Reyes: so in plain terms, INT8 wins on latency/cost; FP8 wins on quality for our extraction-heavy prompts. is that consistent across sequences of 1k tokens?
[05:52] Jordan Park: FP8 advantage shrinks as sequences shorten; at 1k tokens you do see more divergence. also caching (we call it KV caching) helps a lot if you have repeated prefixes. if your RAG uses similar context chunks the delta narrows.
[06:20] Maya Reyes: we do have a lot of repeated system prompt and instruction tokens, so KV cache might help. what's the caveat there?
[06:30] Jordan Park: cache hits reduce compute but add complexity around freshness and invalidation. Optimize recommends caching prefixes below a certain variability threshold and will surface hit rate metrics.
[07:05] Priya Kumar: curious about regressions — if we deploy INT8 and see quality dip, can we auto-roll back or fallback to FP8?
[07:15] Avery Chen: yes, rollouts support canary and automatic fallback policies. you can route a small % to FP8 profile if quality metrics dip beyond a threshold.
[07:40] Owen Li: curious on instrumentation — what traces/logs do you need from us to run the benchmarks close to prod?
[07:48] Jordan Park: sample inference traces with prompt+response pairs and timing. ideally a few thousand calls representative of peak traffic. also include desired SLO and any blacklist/whitelist of prompt types.
[08:20] Maya Reyes: we can export traces from our staging. are there format constraints?
[08:27] Jordan Park: simple JSONL with fields: prompt, response, timestamp, latency — but don't worry i will send a template.
[08:45] Maya Reyes: perfect. can you talk through cost deltas? roughly how much cheaper is INT8?
[08:52] Jordan Park: ballpark — if you normalize to tokens, INT8 can be 20-40% cheaper than FP8 depending on model and kernel. Optimizer's suggested batching and kernel selection also affect that. for a Dedicated pricing model we can show you unit economics in the console.
[09:22] Priya Kumar: on Dedicated, what's the SLA? and is there an option to burst to hosted?
[09:30] Avery Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA for uptime and latency tiers; burst to hosted is an available policy for overflow but there are data residency considerations. we'll outline options in the pricing doc.
[10:00] Jordan Park: demoing the quality vs latency slider — you can pick a target latency and Optimize will recommend a quant profile + batching + kernel hints. here's an example: set p95 target 350ms, it recommended INT8 + batch 4 + cached prefixes for our sample workload.
[10:35] Maya Reyes: did you run those with our traces or synthetic?
[10:38] Jordan Park: synthetic tuned to match your distribution; results will shift with your actual traces.
[11:05] Maya Reyes: for the pilot, we want to validate both throughput and hallucination/regression on a held-out test. what's the typical timeframe for getting results back?
[11:14] Jordan Park: once we get traces and access, initial benchmark report in 3-5 business days for standard runs; if we need custom instrumentation maybe a week.
[11:30] Owen Li: what's the overhead for FP8 in terms of GPU memory and instance type?
[11:37] Jordan Park: FP8 has slightly higher memory footprint but can be executed efficiently on recent GPU kernels; in some cases we recommend a different instance SKU. Optimize will surface compatible instance types.
[12:05] Maya Reyes: any unexpected edge cases you've seen with INT8? like hallucinations on extraction?
[12:13] Jordan Park: sometimes degeneracy on very specialized prompts — that's where fp8 or partial quantization helps. also quantization-aware tuning and post-quant fine-tune steps reduce those failures.
[12:40] Priya Kumar: what's the support model during pilot? dedicated SE or on-call?
[12:46] Avery Chen: pilot includes SE support for onboarding and benchmark analysis; dedicated plans have enhanced support SLAs.
[13:05] Jordan Park: quick note on tooling — we log per-token latencies, per-route cost breakdowns, and have a regression alerting pipeline tied to your eval sets. so if INT8 deployment causes score drop we can trigger an alert and rollback.
[13:40] Maya Reyes: good. about data residency: we have EU customers, do you support region-specific Dedicated?
[13:49] Avery Chen: yes we have EU regions and can pin Dedicated capacity to specific regions. Private on-prem is also an option for strict residency.
[14:10] Owen Li: will the pilot include tests for concurrency and cold-start latencies?
[14:18] Jordan Park: yes we can run burst tests and cold-start profiles; Optimize simulates both.
[14:45] Maya Reyes: i noticed in previous docs you mentioned 'KV cash' in one slide — just flag that was a typo, but we understand you mean KV cache.
[14:55] Jordan Park: ha yeah classic speech-to-text mixup, thanks for flag.
[15:10] Jordan Park: showing an example dashboard — quality delta by prompt bucket, latency histogram, and a table of recommended quant profiles per route.
[15:40] Priya Kumar: about eval sets — can we plug our automated tests into your regression pipeline?
[15:47] Jordan Park: yes, we support uploading custom eval suites, automated scoring and scheduled runs.
[16:10] Maya Reyes: OK let's talk pilot scope specifics — we want to test: 1) INT8 vs FP8 on our extraction tasks, 2) KV cache impact on repeated prompts, 3) concurrency at peak qps, and 4) regression on hallucination metrics.
[16:29] Avery Chen: sounds good. recommended pilot: 2 weeks, run in Dedicated staging with your KMS and VPC, we'll provide benchmark report and recommended profile.
[16:44] Owen Li: timeline-wise Jan 5 start works if we can get the template and a runbook this week.
[16:52] Jordan Park: will send template and runbook today, and a spreadsheet for benchmark results.
[17:10] Priya Kumar: pricing — we need a rough estimate for 2-week pilot and then monthly Dedicated.
[17:20] Avery Chen: i'll include pilot pricing (reduced) and monthly Dedicated tiers in the follow-up.
[17:35] Maya Reyes: any risks we should be aware of?
[17:40] Jordan Park: quantization can occasionally introduce low-frequency regressions; we recommend a staged rollout and solid eval suites. also kernel availability on older hardware can affect performance.
[18:00] Maya Reyes: ok pros/cons captured. one last question on tool calling and structured output — do quant profiles affect determinism?
[18:10] Jordan Park: quantization can affect deterministic outputs slightly; if you need strict determinism we recommend using fp8 or running a validation pass.
[18:40] Priya Kumar: can you include an example of the console config we'll need to change for each route?
[18:47] Jordan Park: yes, i'll include a config snippet in the runbook.
[19:05] Owen Li: anything else on compliance? we need SOC2 evidence and a contact for security questionnaire.
[19:12] Avery Chen: security pack will include SOC2 summary, SAML/SSO notes, KMS integration docs and a security contact — i'll attach in the follow-up.
[19:32] Maya Reyes: great. let's recap next steps.
[19:36] Avery Chen: recap: send INT8/FP8 benchmark spreadsheet, share runbook and template for traces, provide pricing, schedule pilot kickoff Jan 5 tentative. Jordan to own runbook, i will own pricing and security pack.
[20:05] Priya Kumar: thanks all.
[20:08] Maya Reyes: thanks, talk soon.
[44:30] [call ends]

Notes: transcript contains occasional ASR errors (product names, 'KV cash') and speaker overlaps. Refer to action_items and next_steps metadata for deliverables.
